transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2025-07-30
Start: 14:00 UTC
Duration: ~48 minutes
Location: Zoom
Recording: Enabled
Attendees: Jordan Myers (Redwood AE), Aisha Khan (Redwood SE), Luis Ortega (Redwood CSM), Maya Chen (Nautilus), Omar Reyes (Nautilus), Priya Nair (Nautilus Procurement)

Summary (auto):
Quick renewal status check, alignment on APAC capacity uplift (burst vs reserved), EU private pilot timeline and KMS/audit requirements, procurement timeline and pricing ask. Agreed next steps include pricing with APAC burst tiers, small throughput benchmark, and security pack.

Topics:
- Renewal / term extension options
- APAC burst capacity vs Dedicated pool
- EU private (VPC) pilot & KMS/HSM requirements
- Security artifacts and procurement timeline
- Benchmark plan and success criteria

Action items (captured):
- See metadata action_items list above.

Transcript body:
[00:00] Jordan (Redwood): all right cool everyone can hear me?
[00:03] Maya (Nautilus): yep we can hear you, thanks jordan.
[00:06] Jordan: great. quick agenda for today: short renewal readout, apac uplift ask from nautilus, eu private pilot questions and then procurement timeline. try to keep it tight.
[00:18] Maya: sounds good. we'll be brief, we have priya for procurement specifics.
[00:22] Aisha (Redwood SE): hi all, i'll be focused on the benchmark and runtime questions.
[00:26] Omar (Nautilus): thanks, from infra side i'll ask about vpc and egress.

[01:10] Jordan: quick renewal context — you folks are up for renewal in september, right? we chatted in the last touch that you're looking at a modest term extension, plus a short pilot in eu for private serving and an apac burst window for peak season. is that still accurate?
[01:22] Maya: yes that's right. our peak booking window is october through december, so apac capacity needs to be in place by mid-september ideally, but we understand provisioning lead times.
[01:34] Priya (Nautilus Procurement): for procurement, timeline is vendor selection by 2025-08-15, PO in by 2025-08-30 if possible. so pricing and the SOW need to be in our hands early.

[02:10] Jordan: understood. okay so option A is a 12-month extension with a small reserved committed pool in us-west + burstable APAC credits; option B is a 9-month bridge with a larger APAC reserved pool and shorter commitment for EU pilot separately. i'll walk through cost deltas after aisha covers feasibility.
[02:35] Aisha: technically both paths are viable. key tradeoffs: reserved APAC capacity guarantees throughput and lower unit cost; burst credits are cheaper to stand up but we can't guarantee cold-start latency if the pool is empty and there is a sudden spike. also if you plan for long-response LLMs, token-mix matters. quick note: our runtime has continuous batching and prefix caching but with apac cold nodes you can see the kv-cache warmup penalty — sometimes transcript said kv cash earlier — sorry audio typo — kv cache.
[03:10] Omar: big q for us is egress and VPC peering. for EU private pilot we must ensure no egress to public internet and our KMS handles keys. does redwood support customer-managed keys and hsm?
[03:25] Luis: yes on the private side — we support bring-your-own-KMS and can integrate with HSM-backed flows. audit logs and object-level encryption are included in the enterprise pack. we'll share the KMS integration matrix.

[03:55] Maya: what about SOC2 scope? our security team wants a snapshot of controls and an iso cert if available.
[04:03] Luis: we have SOC2 Type II and ISO27001; i'll attach redacted reports and our control matrix. we can also provide audit log samples with redacted ids.

[04:30] Priya: pricing — we need a clear per-token estimate for generation and embeddings, and line items for reserved GPU pool vs burst credits. also any one-time setup for EU private pilot.
[04:45] Jordan: yes we'll send a revised quote with three scenarios: conservative (lower reserved + burst), aggressive (higher reserved APAC + discounts), and pilot-only (EU private for 3 months). include one-time onboarding and kms integration fees.

[06:00] Aisha: on the benchmark — recommended test is a 4-hour window with realistic query mix: 60% short prompts (50-150 tokens), 30% medium (150-600), 10% long (>600). we'll run the throughput test on apac nodes and capture p95 latency and cold/warm behavior. expecting p95 around 350-450ms for short prompts if warm; cold can spike.
[06:30] Omar: can we request a scripted test using our prompt templates? we don't want synthetic-only.
[06:36] Aisha: absolutely. maya, if you can share top 20 prompt templates and an anonymized dataset of tokens, we'll bake that into the benchmark.
[06:44] Maya: yep will do, i'll scrub PII and share by tuesday.

[07:10] Jordan: procurement asks: priya when you say vendor selection 8/15, is that flexible if we need to add a short security review?
[07:18] Priya: it's firm but we have a 48-hour window to review final docs. worst case we need a short security call the week of 8/11.

[08:00] Omar: question on fallback: if apac capacity is saturated, can traffic be routed to us-west with some routing policy and accept higher latency? we need failover for availability.
[08:12] Aisha: yes, smart routing supports policy-based fallback. you can set max-latency thresholds and fallback to lower-cost models or other regions. note that cross-region egress will add latency and egress costs.

[08:45] Maya: on the EU private pilot: expected timeline? we want vpc peering, kms, and audit logs within four weeks of sign. is that realistic?
[08:56] Luis: for a small-scale pilot (1-2 GPU nodes) that's doable in 3-5 weeks depending on your firewall and networking approvals. HSM/KMS integration typically adds an extra week for security review.

[10:15] Jordan: procurement alignment — we'll prepare a minimal SOW for the pilot and a separate SOW for the reserved capacity. both can be amendments under one master agreement to speed signing.
[10:27] Priya: that helps. can you include sample SLAs for uptime and token throughput?
[10:33] Jordan: yes standard dedicated SLA and dedicated capacity uptime of 99.9% for GS1 pools, we'll include latency targets per model family.

[12:00] Maya: security nuance — our compliance team will want to know how long data is retained in logs and whether we can opt-out of certain telemetry.
[12:10] Luis: yes retention is configurable; default 90 days for detailed traces, we can increase or redact per contract. we'll note that in the security pack.

[13:00] Aisha: quick technical note — if you plan to quantize models for cost savings, there are throughput/latency tradeoffs and some quality delta. we can recommend quantization profiles per workload once we see your prompt set.
[13:18] Omar: do you support on-prem option if the EU pilot requires fully air-gapped?
[13:24] Luis: yes we have an on-prem package but that moves from a pilot to a longer procurement cycle — provisioning and licensing differ. for the pilot it's easier to do VPC private serving.

[14:05] Maya: let's talk numbers briefly, without getting into final quote — what's the delta in unit cost reserved vs burst?
[14:12] Jordan: ballpark: reserved reduces per-token cost by ~20-35% depending on utilization; burst credits are ~10-15% higher per token but cheaper upfront and flexible. we'll model three utilization cases in the quote.

[15:00] Priya: procurement also needs PO terms and invoicing cadence — monthly vs quarterly — preferences?
[15:07] Jordan: we default to monthly invoicing but we can accommodate quarterly invoicing for enterprise customers; we'll add a line item for invoicing cadence options.

[17:00] Maya: success criteria for the pilot — what should we measure?
[17:07] Aisha: suggested: 1) p95 latency under agreed thresholds for warm traffic, 2) throughput target (rps/tokens/sec), 3) model output quality measured by a small eval suite (we can run redwood eval harness against your prompts), 4) incident response time during pilot. if those hit targets, we auto-roll the eu pilot into reserved capacity.
[17:40] Omar: how do we measure quality regression if you change model version?
[17:46] Aisha: we keep eval baselines per prompt set and will alert on regression. also we support canary rollouts and A/B traffic routing.

[19:00] Maya: one risk — apac provider availability: you've had outages reported in the past with some cloud partners; will that be addressed?
[19:10] Jordan: yes we will include failover plans and fallback to alternate regions; also provide a runbook for incident windows.

[21:00] Priya: ok procurement checkpoint — if you send pricing and security pack by monday 8/4 we can proceed with an internal audit and finalize vendor selection 8/15.
[21:10] Jordan: confirmed, we'll aim for 8/4.

[22:00] Maya: small question on ticketing and on-call — do we get a dedicated CSM during onboarding?
[22:07] Luis: yes, for pilots we assign a CSM and an engineering onboarding contact; post-onboarding SLA varies by contract tier.

[24:00] Omar: networking specifics — we will share firewall rules and nat egress constraints; is there an IP allowlist?
[24:10] Aisha: yes we provide IP ranges for region nodes; for private VPC we do peering and you won't need our public range except for management plane which can be whitelisted.

[26:00] Jordan: can we run through the proposed timeline briefly?
[26:05] Jordan: 8/4 - proposal and security pack delivered; 8/5-8/11 - internal security review (nautilus); 8/11 - optional deep security call if needed; 8/15 - vendor selection; 8/18-8/30 - PO and SOW sign; 9/1-9/20 - provisioning and pilot run; mid-september apac burst live.
[26:40] Priya: that fits our constraints.

[28:00] Maya: any blockers on your side?
[28:05] Jordan: only dependency is your prompt set for the benchmark and your network team sign-off.
[28:10] Maya: we'll prioritize that.

[30:00] Aisha: small gotcha — when we test apac nodes, make sure the workload's token distribution matches production otherwise the p95 will be optimistic.
[30:08] Omar: agreed.

[32:00] Jordan: competitors — you mentioned evaluating bigcloud ai and shipserve labs; anything specific driving those short-lists?
[32:07] Maya: mainly price and local region presence for apac. shipserve had a good demo on logistics-specific models but lacked the observability we need.

[34:00] Jordan: thanks, we'll emphasize observability and rollout controls in the docs.

[36:00] Maya: final ask — can you include a short worksheet in the quote that shows cost sensitivity to utilization (40/60/80%)? procurement loves that.
[36:10] Jordan: yes we'll include a utilization worksheet.

[38:00] Priya: also include contract termination clause and data residency terms for the eu pilot.
[38:06] Luis: will do.

[40:00] Jordan: recap of next steps: 1) jordan to send quote + utilization worksheet + security pack by 8/4, 2) aisha to schedule and run apac benchmark with nautilus prompt set and share results by 8/8, 3) luis to send KMS integration matrix and retention options by 8/6, 4) nautilus to share prompt templates and firewall rules by 8/5.
[40:25] Maya: confirmed.

[41:00] Priya: if everything lines up, procurement will issue PO by 8/30.

[42:00] Jordan: great. any quick questions before we close?
[42:05] Omar: quick on SSO — sso via SAML? we use azure ad.
[42:10] Luis: yes SAML SSO via Azure AD is supported; we'll include SAML docs.

[44:00] Maya: thanks everyone, appreciate the quick readout.
[44:05] Jordan: thanks all, we'll follow up with the deliverables.
[44:10] Aisha: bye.
[44:12] Priya: bye.

[48:00] End of meeting (recording stopped)
